questionTextEnglish: Under section 5, what kinds of facts may generally be proved?
optionsEnglish: Every fact a party wants to mention
Facts in issue and facts declared relevant by the Act
Only facts admitted by the other party
explanationEnglish: Section 5 limits evidence to facts in issue and other facts declared relevant by the Act.

questionTextEnglish: Which principle is expressed in section 6?
explanationEnglish: Section 6 treats facts forming part of the same transaction as relevant, even if they occurred at different times or places.

questionTextEnglish: What does section 60 require for oral evidence?
optionsEnglish: It must be corroborated by two witnesses
explanationEnglish: Section 60 requires direct oral evidence from a person who personally perceived the fact.

questionTextEnglish: Which section directs proof of digital-record contents according to section 65B?
explanationEnglish: Section 65A states that contents of digital records may be proved in accordance with section 65B.

questionTextEnglish: Who must prove facts asserted as the basis of a requested judgment under section 101?
explanationEnglish: Section 101 places the burden on the person who asserts the facts on which the requested judgment depends.

questionTextEnglish: Under section 25, may a confession made to a police-officer be proved against the person accused of an offence?
optionsEnglish: No - it shall not be proved as against the accused
Only if the accused signed it
explanationEnglish: Section 25: no confession made to a police-officer shall be proved as against a person accused of any offence.

questionTextEnglish: Under section 26, a confession made while the accused is in police custody can be proved only if made in the immediate presence of whom?
explanationEnglish: Section 26 excludes confessions made in police custody unless made in the immediate presence of a Magistrate (the Explanation limits who counts as a Magistrate).

questionTextEnglish: Under section 24, a confession in a criminal proceeding is irrelevant if caused by an inducement, threat or promise proceeding from whom?
explanationEnglish: Section 24 requires the inducement, threat or promise to have reference to the charge and to proceed from a person in authority.

questionTextEnglish: Section 32(1) makes relevant a statement by a person about which matter?
optionsEnglish: The cause of his death or circumstances of the transaction that resulted in his death
explanationEnglish: Section 32(1) covers statements as to the cause of death, or any circumstances of the transaction which resulted in death, where the cause of death comes into question.

questionTextEnglish: Under section 32(1), must the maker have been under expectation of death when the statement was made?
optionsEnglish: No - such statements are relevant whether or not he was under expectation of death
Only if made to a Magistrate
explanationEnglish: The text of s.32(1) says such statements are relevant whether or not the person was under expectation of death, whatever the nature of the proceeding.

questionTextEnglish: Under section 102, on whom does the burden of proof in a suit or proceeding lie?
optionsEnglish: The person who would fail if no evidence at all were given on either side
explanationEnglish: Section 102 places the burden on the person who would fail if no evidence were given on either side.

questionTextEnglish: Under section 106, who must prove a fact that is especially within the knowledge of a person?
explanationEnglish: Section 106: when any fact is especially within the knowledge of any person, the burden of proving that fact is upon him.

questionTextEnglish: What does section 115 prevent a person from doing?
optionsEnglish: Denying the truth of a thing he intentionally caused another to believe and act upon
explanationEnglish: Estoppel (s.115): a person who by declaration, act or omission intentionally caused another to believe a thing and act on it cannot deny its truth in a suit or proceeding between them or their representatives.

questionTextEnglish: Under section 118, who is competent to testify?
optionsEnglish: All persons, unless prevented from understanding questions or giving rational answers (by tender years, extreme old age, disease or similar cause)
Only persons who take an oath in Court
explanationEnglish: Section 118 makes all persons competent unless the Court considers they are so prevented; a lunatic is not incompetent unless prevented by lunacy (Explanation).

questionTextEnglish: Section 122 protects which kind of communication?
optionsEnglish: Communications between spouses made during marriage
explanationEnglish: Section 122: a person who is or has been married cannot be compelled (or, without consent, permitted) to disclose a communication made during marriage, subject to the exceptions in the section.

questionTextEnglish: Under section 126, an Advocate may disclose client communications made in the course of employment only with what?
optionsEnglish: His client's express consent (subject to the Provisos)
explanationEnglish: Section 126 bars disclosure unless with the client's express consent, subject to the provisos in the section.

questionTextEnglish: What does "conclusive proof" mean under section 4?
optionsEnglish: The Court may call for more proof
On proof of one fact, the Court shall regard the other as proved and not allow evidence to disprove it
The fact is presumed until disproved
explanationEnglish: Section 4: when one fact is declared conclusive proof of another, the Court shall on proof of the one regard the other as proved and shall not allow evidence to disprove it.

questionTextEnglish: Under section 45 (as amended in 2022), whose opinions are relevant on points such as foreign law, science, physical or forensic evidence or digital record, art, handwriting or finger impression?
optionsEnglish: Persons specially skilled in the matter (experts)
explanationEnglish: Section 45: the opinions of persons specially skilled in the relevant field are relevant facts; such persons are called experts.
